chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who married a girl, so he consummated the marriage with her. Then he was tested with her mother and committed fornication with her. Would his wife be prohibited to him? He said: No. Indeed, the permissible is not prohibited by the prohibition.
ai.seo_question: Does fornication with a wife's mother prohibit the wife from her husband?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between *mahramiyyah* by marriage (*bi-al-irbah*) and *mahramiyyah* by blood or fornication (*bi-al-zina*), affirming that the latter does not sever the former. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) applies the legal maxim that the prohibition of fornication does not annul the validity of the existing marital contract, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence for determining permanent vs. temporary prohibitions. This ruling ensures that a man remains married to his wife even if he commits illicit relations with her mother, distinguishing it from cases where fornication creates a new barrier.
